topics.name: Protein Structure Prediction and Its Evaluation
topics.definition: Predicting a protein's 3D structure from its amino-acid sequence; AlphaFold 2/3 and RoseTTAFold are the landmark learned models, and the critical question is what their evaluation established and what it did not.
topics.explanation: The 'protein folding problem' - inferring native structure from sequence - stood for decades until DeepMind's AlphaFold 2 (Jumper et al., Nature 2021) reached near-experimental accuracy on the CASP14 blind assessment, and RoseTTAFold (Baek et al., Science 2021) independently showed similar performance with a simpler tr-track architecture. AlphaFold 3 (Abramson et al., Nature 2024) extended to complexes with ligands, nucleic acids, and modified residues using a diffusion-based module over atom coordinates. What the evaluation did establish: on single-domain and well-sampled targets, per-residue (GDT_TS/TM-score) prediction is near-experimental, so structure prediction for many proteins is effectively solved as a benchmark task. What it did not establish: 'solved folding' as physics - AlphaFold is a coevolution-and-structure-attention predictor that does not simulate the energy landscape, does not guarantee it can handle unseen folds, dynamics, disordered regions, induced fit, or mutant/condition-dependent conformations, and its confidence (pLDDT) can miscalibrate on novel families. CASP itself is partly an overfitting-vulnerable benchmark (evolving MSA databases, homology leakage), so real-world generalization to never-seen superfold types or to function-relevant conformational ensembles remains open. Independent critiques ('Assessing AlphaFold...' style work, e.g. on cases where predicted structures disagreed with experiment for specific mutants/families) reinforced that high aggregate scores coexist with important failures. The honest framing is that it is a landmark empirical achievement whose evaluation measured a narrow, benchmark-defined problem extremely well.
learning_objectives: Summarize how AF2 (Evoformer + structure module) and RoseTTAFold predict structure.
State what CASP14 performance established and what 'folding' claims go beyond it.
Explain why high GDT_TS can coexist with failures on dynamics, disorder, and novel folds.
Discuss benchmark limitations (homology leakage, overfitting) in protein-structure eval.
math_foundations: Distance/angle representations in a pair graph
common_misconceptions: AlphaFold solved protein folding; it solved a benchmark prediction task, not the physics/dynamics problem.
High pLDDT guarantees correctness on new families; it can miscalibrate out of distribution.
AF predicts conformational dynamics and induced fit; it generally predicts a static native-like state.

topics.name: Generative Models for Molecules and Materials and Their Evaluation Pitfalls
topics.definition: Models that propose new molecular or material structures (VAEs, GANs, flows, diffusion, RL), optimized to maximize a target property while respecting valence; evaluation is notoriously prone to metrics that reward artifacts over real discoveries.
topics.explanation: Molecular generation operates in SMILES/graph/coordinate space. Classic VAE/RNN-over-SMILES and GFlowNet/RL approaches (e.g. GuacaMol/GFlowNet-EM, JT-VAE) optimize for novelty, diversity, and property scores. Diffusion over 3D coordinates with symmetry-aware networks - EDM (Hoogeboom et al., ICML 2022), and score-based models like DiffDock for docking - generate physically structured candidates directly. The evaluation pitfalls are the load-bearing lesson: distributional-learning metrics that reward 'many valid molecules' or 'high QED/novelty' can be gamed, and a model that produces valid, novel, high-scoring molecules in simulation may be useless if those molecules are un-synthesizable. Synthesis reachability (e.g. Synthetic Accessibility scores, SCScore, or template-free retrosynthesis-based filters) is therefore a required additional axis; a molecule that scores high but no chemist can make is not a discovery. Other traps: reward-hacking a scoring oracle, overfitting to a docking/energy proxy, dataset leakage between train and 'novel' test molecules, and evaluating with the same model used for generation. Honest scientific-ML for molecules/materials therefore reports synthesizability, experimental or high-level-theory validation, and out-of-distribution tests rather than leaderboard proxy scores alone - the same Goodhart logic as adversarial/reward-hacking work, applied to chemistry.
learning_objectives: Describe VAE/flow/diffusion-based molecular generation and the symmetry considerations for 3D diffusion.
Explain why novelty/diversity/validity metrics alone mislead.
Define synthesis reachability and why it is an evaluation must.
Identify reward-hacking and data-leakage risks in generative-chemistry evals.
common_misconceptions: High validity+novelty+QED means useful molecules; synthesis reachability can be ignored at peril.
A docking/reward oracle is ground truth; models happily overfit to it (reward hacking).
Generated 'novel' molecules never appear in training; leakage and scaffold recycling are common.

topics.name: Data-Driven Weather and Climate Forecasting
topics.definition: ML models that forecast weather (GraphCast, Pangu-Weather, GenCast) from atmospheric state, learning patterns from reanalysis data; the central claim is about speed and skill, not replacing physics-based numerical weather prediction.
topics.explanation: Numerical weather prediction (NWP) integrates the primitive equations on a grid with parameterizations of sub-grid processes; it is accurate but computationally heavy. Data-driven forecasters learn the state-to-next-state map: GraphCast (Lam et al., Science 2023) is a message-passing GNN trained on ERA5 reanalysis that beat the operational ECMWF HRES ensemble on most verified variables at a fraction of the compute; Pangu-Weather (Bi et al., Nature 2023) uses 3D Swin-transformers and showed similar skill; GenCast (Price et al., Nature 2024) generates probabilistic forecasts with a diffusion model, capturing spread better than a single deterministic run. Why they are not a physics replacement: they are trained on reanalysis - a blend of observations and NWP - so their 'supervision' is the physics model's own output; their skill degrades on extreme events, rare phenomena, and variables poorly represented in training; they can violate conservation and produce physically inconsistent trajectories on long horizons; and their value is not yet established for climate (decadal, trend) forecasting, which is about statistics of an evolving system, not single trajectories. The realistic picture: fast, strong short-to-medium-range forecasts and ensemble members that can inform downstream decisions, but they rely on physics data for training and validation, do not guarantee physical consistency, and should be treated as complements to, and cross-checked against, NWP - the same in-distribution caveat as neural operators.
learning_objectives: Describe GraphCast, Pangu, and GenCast architectures and their headline skill/compute claims.
Explain why training on reanalysis ties ML forecasters to physics models.
State why skill on verified variables does not imply reliability on extremes or climate.
Argue the complement-not-replacement position with conservation/consistency reasoning.
common_misconceptions: These models replace physics NWP; they are trained on reanalysis built partly by NWP and lack guaranteed physical consistency.
Skill on standard verified variables equals climate reliability; extremes and trends remain open.
Faster always means better; speed helps but validation against physics is essential.

further_reading.title: Learning Skillful Medium-Range Global Forecasting (GraphCast)
Accurate Medium-range Global Weather Forecasting with Deep Learning (Pangu-Weather)

topics.name: Genomics, Single-Cell, and Astronomy Machine Learning
topics.definition: Foundation and task models for biological sequence/cell data (single-cell omics, gene regulation) and for astronomical signals (surveys, transients, galaxies), where ML handles massive, high-dimensional observation streams.
topics.explanation: In genomics, sequence models like DNABERT, Nucleotide Transformers, and Enformer (Attention-based models over the genome) learn regulatory signals from DNA, and single-cell foundation models aim to generalize across cell atlases: scVI (Lopez et al.) provides a probabilistic latent model for single-cell RNA-seq (a long-standing classical method), while newer transformer-based 'scGPT'/'GeneFormer'-style models treat cells or gene expression as sequences/tokens to pre-train foundation models - the claim is cross-dataset transfer, but these are young, and the field has not yet established which capabilities are real versus overfit to benchmark atlases. In astronomy, ML handles survey-scale data: transient/galaxy classification (e.g. the 'M6'/'AstroNN' and GalNet lines of work), gravitational-wave and exoplanet detection, and cosmological parameter inference - where density-estimation/neural-posterior-estimation methods learn complex likelihoods from simulations; these are powerful for classification and simulation-based inference but depend on simulation realism and can be poor at physical extrapolation. In all three, the epistemics echo AI-for-science broadly: strong in-distribution benchmark gains, uncertain out-of-distribution and physical/mechanistic reliability. Because the specific recent papers and claims here are fast-moving and harder to pin to stable canonical citations, this topic names the methods honestly and flags single-cell foundation models and astronomy simulators as an active, partly-hypothesized area rather than established capability.
learning_objectives: Describe single-cell latent models (scVI) and the ambition of single-cell foundation models.
Give a genomics sequence-model example (Enformer) and what it predicts.
Explain simulation-based inference and neural density estimation in astronomy/cosmology.
State why these are early/hypothesis-heavy and how to read such claims.
common_misconceptions: Single-cell foundation models are proven to transfer across all datasets; evidence is early and benchmark-bound.
Astronomy ML 'understands' physics; it fits simulation-derived patterns.
Sequence-model accuracy equals biological understanding.

further_reading.title: Deep Generative and Discriminative Models for Single-cell Gene Expression (scVI)

topics.name: AI for Mathematics: Theorem Proving, Formalisation, and Conjecture Generation
topics.definition: Applying ML to mathematics: automated theorem proving in proof assistants, formalisation of informal proofs, proof search (tactics), and conjecture generation, with a track record that includes both genuine results and hype.
topics.explanation: Two regimes exist. Formal mathematics is verifiable: proof assistants (Lean, Coq) reduce checking to machine-verified proofs, so an ML system that produces a valid Lean proof has a hard correctness guarantee - this is where real wins land. AlphaGeometry (Trinh et al., Nature 2024) combined a symbolic deduction engine with a neural 'candidate-construction' module to solve Olympiad-style geometry problems, and AlphaProof/AlphaGeometry 2 (Hubert et al., Nature 2025) learned to interact with formal languages (Lean) and reached IMO-medal-level performance on problems that had been formalised, using Monte-Carlo-tree-search-style proof search guided by a learned value model plus reinforcement learning on formal statements. Earlier work (Lample et al. 'Harnessing neural networks for mathematics', and the GPT-f/Graph-tactics line for automated reasoning in Lean/Coq) showed transformers can produce proof tactics and conjectures. The honest track record is mixed: on formalised problems, verifiable success is real and strong; but conjecture generation (Liet et al., Funs, and the DeepMind 'FunSearch'/'Aletheia' line, plus co-works such as finding the cap-set or knot-theory invariants via AlphaTensor) yields a handful of novel, validated results among many plausible-but-trivial or human-selected ones, and much of what 'AI did math' marketing implies overstates the rate and significance of new theorems. The epistemics: formal verification is a rare gold standard in science, so ML-math claims should be weighed by how many results are actually machine-verified and independently deemed non-trivial - which remains a small fraction.
learning_objectives: Explain why formal (Lean/Coq) results carry a verifiability advantage over informal claims.
Describe AlphaGeometry's neuro-symbolic split (construction vs deduction).
Summarize AlphaProof/AlphaGeometry-2 formal-reasoning results and limits.
Weave conjecture-generation results against hype with an honest track record.
common_misconceptions: 'AI proved new mathematics' usually means machine-verified novel results; many outputs are trivial or human-curated.
Formal proofs are self-evidently deep; verifiability guarantees correctness, not significance.
Olympiad-geometry success generalizes to open research mathematics today; the frontier remains mostly human.

Advanced Functional Mathematical Reasoning and Discovery (AlphaProof/AlphaGeometry 2)
Harnessing Neural Networks for Mathematics
